newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus court rejects Slovenian cash claim on bank.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus court rejects Slovenian cash claim on bank.

text.p: A Cyprus court on Tuesday rejected a claim by Slovenia seeking to recover millions of dollars which it said the national bank of former Yugoslavia might have deposited in a bank on the island.

"Slovenia alleged that the accounts of the National Bank of Yugoslavia with Beogradska Banka Cyprus contained funds belonging to Slovenian banks and citizens but failed to support this with evidence," Beogradska Banka said in a statement issued in Nicosia.

The government of Slovenia filed a court action in Cyprus last year claiming that the now-defunct national bank of former Yugoslavia could have stashed millions of marks that belonged to Slovenes in an account at the offshore branch of Beogradska Banka in Cyprus.
The claim was for 900 million marks ($480 million), which it said was deposited in the national bank before the break-up of former Yugoslavia.
The Nicosia district court had issued an interlocutory order blocking all accounts of the national bank with Beogradska Banka pending the outcome of the case.
The court order was issued in the absence of Beogradska Banka, which later contested the order in court.

"After a long trial that lasted almost one year, the court issued today its decision and cancelled in full the interlocutory order and dismissed the application of Slovenia with costs being adjudged against Slovenia," the Beogradska Banka statement said.

The court ruling, according to Beogradska Banka, stated that Slovenia failed to comply with its legal duty when applying to the court in the absence of defendants to make a full and frank disclosure of the relevant facts and the nature of their claim.
The Cypriot lawyers who represented Slovenia in the case were not immediately available for comment.
